 Prabowo apologises to Malaysia and Singapore over transboundary haze
 By ARFA YUNUS 
 Monday, 16 Nov 2026
 | 8:18 AM MYT

 Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., center, and first lady Louise Araneta-Marcos pose for a photo with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto during the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila, Philippines Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. (Ezra Acayan/Pool Photo via AP) 
 MANILA: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto has apologised to Malaysia and Singapore over the transboundary haze caused by forest and land fires in his country, assuring that Jakarta is taking firm action against companies responsible for the blazes.
 Prabowo said the Indonesian government was doing its utmost to contain the fires, which have been raging for nearly four months, while acknowledging their impact on neighbouring countries.
 He said this during his intervention at the plenary session of the 49th Asean Summit here on Sunday (Nov 15), according to Indonesian news portal Kompas.com.
 The session was also attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Sultan of Brunei Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and leaders and representatives of other Asean member states.
 Prabowo said Indonesia would not tolerate corporations implicated in the fires, with enforcement measures already taken against several companies.
 “We have revoked 17 concessions from companies. Currently, 26 companies are under investigation.
 “Eleven companies have been charged. Twenty-three other companies are on the list to be charged.
 “In total, 104 companies are under investigation by our police,” he said.
 Prabowo said Indonesia had also mobilised 71,000 personnel to combat the fires, although the operations had come at a heavy human and financial cost.
 “We have deployed 71,000 forest firefighters. We lost 16 people who died, and many more were injured while battling the fire. We also lost two helicopters,” he said.
 Despite the extensive firefighting operations, Prabowo acknowledged that the resulting haze had crossed national borders, affecting communities in Malaysia and Singapore.
 He also stressed the need for Indonesia to adopt a more systematic approach to managing forest and land fires, with greater emphasis on prevention rather than relying primarily on firefighting and mitigation measures.
 To this end, Prabowo said the Indonesian government was preparing to establish a new agency and introduce programmes to strengthen wildfire prevention efforts.
 The measures are expected to improve Indonesia’s ability to prevent future fires and minimise their impact on neighbouring countries.
